doc.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

title: Playing in Jon Faddis's Carnegie Hall band
summary: He describes the Carnegie Hall Jazz Band's concerts, tours, personnel and trumpet section.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: And what’s your weeks like these days? Playing different kinds of things now?

Well I still have — a variety of stuff happens, it’s wonderful. I play in the Carnegie Hall band that Jon Faddis leads, and we do four concerts a year in Carnegie Hall and then we’ve been getting some more outside work. We went to Japan year before last for a week to a festival. And we went to South America this past November for ten days and we’re going to Mexico City in a couple of weeks. And we do some of the festivals in Europe in the summer, the well traveled path. And more and more stuff is coming up. And every concert is different because there’s new music written for each concert. It’s really interesting. It really keeps you on your toes. And Jon is developing into an excellent band leader now. His experience with Thad helped him quite a bit. So maybe if you get a chance you might—
Talk to him, yeah. Who else is playing in that group?
Well in the saxophones there’s Frank Wess and Dick Oatts, Ralph LaLama, Gary Smulyan. Slide Hampton’s in the band and he writes for the band too which is —
We know that. We heard that the other night.

Oh yes, well you know he’s been a good writer for a long time and he’s just wonderful. He’s still growing. It’s wonderful. It’s great. The trumpet section of that band is always great because they have Lew Soloff and Earl Gardner and Byron Stripling and Randy Brecker. If you want to have a successful — I always tell the arrangers if you want a successful arrangement with this band just write the trumpets in unison and it’s going to sound like no other band in the world. And then with Jon too then you have five. Oh it’s © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
unbelievable. So he gets the best guys that are available to play in the band, which is really good.
